summary: This unit teaches you to facilitate access to external services: finding out what guests need, choosing licensed suppliers, arranging transfers, tours, restaurants, medical help and other services, keeping guests safe, handling costs in J$ and US$, writing confirmations and logs, and putting problems right.

blocks.p: Guests at a villa or small property rarely stay inside the gates. They want to see a waterfall, take a boat trip, eat at a restaurant, rent a car, find a doctor or have a suit cleaned. Most of these services are provided by **outside businesses**, called external services. This unit teaches you to find out what the guest needs, choose a safe and suitable supplier, book it, confirm it, record it and put problems right. It is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees.

When you arrange an outside service, the guest trusts **you** and the property, not only the supplier. If a tour is unsafe or a taxi does not come, the guest blames the villa. Honest advice, careful checking and good records protect the guest and the property.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: two theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and two practical tasks. In the first you arrange a tour and an airport transfer in a role play, using an approved supplier list, booking forms, confirmation slips and a log. In the second you make a guest services directory and handle requests for a doctor, a pharmacy, a babysitter and dry cleaning. The assessor watches your questions, your choice of supplier, your records and your care for privacy.

sections.title: Finding out the guest needs and choosing suppliers

head: Type
Examples
rows: Transport
Airport transfers, taxis, minibuses, car hire, ferries, flights
Tours and attractions
River rafting, waterfalls, boat and snorkel trips, plantation and coffee tours, cultural shows
Food and entertainment
Restaurant tables, private chefs, nightlife, event hire
Health
Doctor, nurse, hospital, pharmacy, dentist
Personal services
Dry cleaning, laundry, hairdresser, massage, babysitting
Equipment hire
Snorkel gear, bicycles, beach chairs, baby equipment

blocks.h: Finding out what the guest needs

blocks.p: A guest who says 'set up something fun for tomorrow' has not told you enough. **Greet politely, give your full attention, and ask open questions.**

head: Ask about
Examples
rows: Interests
Beaches, adventure, history, food, shopping, quiet time?
Who is going
How many adults and children (ages); anyone who is elderly or has a disability?
Date and time
Which day, what time, how long do they have?
Budget
A price range; whether they want a private or shared service
Special needs
Access, diet, health, fear of water, language
What they have done
What they enjoyed before, what they want to avoid

blocks.p: Write down the answers and **repeat them back**. Then offer **two or three suitable choices** and let the guest decide. Do not choose for the guest.
A good villa keeps an **approved supplier list** of tour, transport and service providers. Use it first. A supplier is added to the list only after checks:

ul: a valid **licence** for the service (for example, a tour or transport operator's licence, or a licensed driver)
**insurance** for passengers and for the activity
vehicles, boats and equipment in good, safe condition, with **life jackets**, seat belts and first aid
clear prices and terms, and reliable contact numbers
good feedback from guests and staff
trained guides and drivers who are polite and honest

blocks.p: The list is checked and updated regularly. Remove any supplier that causes safety problems or complaints. Recommending only approved suppliers saves time, gives the same reliable advice to every guest and protects the villa's name.

blocks.note: Team Jamaica is customer-service training for people who work with visitors. It is run by the Tourism Product Development Company (TPDCo). Know the local area well, so you can give correct directions and advice.
blocks.label: Jamaica

ul: A guest who uses a **wheelchair**: ask first whether the attraction has ramps and accessible toilets and paths. Do not book places with steep steps or rough tracks.
A family with a **small child**: check minimum ages and weights, and whether life jackets and car seats fit.
A guest with a **health condition**: ask what help they need and whether the activity is suitable; suggest they ask their doctor if unsure.
A guest who is **elderly or who tires easily**: choose shorter trips with rest stops and shade.

blocks.p: If a guest asks for a service that is not available in the area, explain politely and **offer the closest alternative**. Never say 'There is nothing to do.'

An **airport transfer** is a booked ride between the airport and the villa. Most guests arrive at Sangster International Airport (Montego Bay) or the Norman Manley International Airport (Kingston), and some use the smaller airports. To book one you need:

ul: the guest's **name and phone number**
the **flight number, date and time** of arrival or departure
the **number of people and bags** (and any large items such as golf clubs or a wheelchair)
the pick-up and drop-off places
child seats, if needed

ol: Take the full details and repeat them back.
Book a licensed operator from the approved list, and agree the **price and currency**.
Get a **booking number** and the driver's contact details.
Record it in the log and give the guest a written confirmation.
**Reconfirm** with the supplier the day before, and check on the day.

blocks.p: For an **arrival**, add the time to leave the aircraft, go through immigration and customs, and collect bags, and then the **drive** to the villa. Guests often need about an hour to clear the airport. Drive times depend on the route and traffic: from Montego Bay to Negril is usually about 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes; to Ocho Rios about 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours. Ask your supplier for the time they allow.

**Example (made-up flight times).** A flight lands at Sangster at 2:00 p.m. The guests need about 1 hour to clear the airport. The drive to the villa is about 1 hour 30 minutes. They will reach the villa at about 2:00 + 1:00 + 1:30 = **4:30 p.m.** Arrange the driver to meet them at about 3:00 p.m., or as the supplier advises.

For a **departure**, work backwards from the flight. International airlines usually ask guests to check in about **3 hours** before the flight, and traffic can be heavy, so the driver should leave early. Always tell the guest the time of the pick-up, in writing.

head: Flight leaves
Check in about
Drive to airport
Latest pick-up (with a 30-minute buffer)
rows: 2:40 p.m. (3 hours before)
1 hour 40 minutes

ul: Call only **licensed, approved taxis**. Agree the fare before the journey if your property does so.
Never send a guest in an unlicensed vehicle.

A guest who wants to **rent a car** needs to show a **valid driver's licence** (from their home country, or an international permit if the company requires), and usually a **credit card** for the deposit. Remind them that people in Jamaica **drive on the left-hand side** of the road, that roads can be narrow and winding, and that they should wear a seat belt.
Guests should check the car, the spare wheel and the insurance, and note any damage on the form before leaving the yard.
Never drive a guest's rental car yourself unless your property's policy and the insurance allow it.

blocks.note: In the rain or at night, rural roads in Jamaica can be dangerous. Advise guests to travel in daylight and to use licensed drivers who know the roads.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: Fares may be in US$ or J$. Tell the guest the price and the currency before the trip. **Use only the villa's exchange rate for that day** if the guest wants to pay in the other currency. Example (made-up rate): a taxi charges J$6,000 each way to the airport. The return trip in total is 6,000 x 2 = **J$12,000**.

Before you recommend a tour, find out what it **includes** (transport, entry, food, drinks, guide), how **long** it takes, the **full cost**, the pick-up and return times and places, the **minimum age** and what the guest must bring.

head: Information to give
Why
rows: Date, pick-up time and place
So the guest is ready
What is included, and the cost and currency
So there are no surprises
How long it lasts and the return time
So the guest can plan the day
What to bring: sun protection, water, shoes, swimwear, cash
So the guest is comfortable and safe
Rules: minimum age, no alcohol before water activities
For safety
The villa's phone number and the company's
So the guest can call if there is a problem

head: Point
Private tour
Shared (group) tour
rows: Who is in it
Only the guest's own party
Several parties, sharing a vehicle and guide
Times and stops
Flexible: the guest can change them
Set times and stops, for all the group
Cost
Higher per person
Lower per person
Best for
Families, couples, guests with access needs or who want a personal service
Single travellers and guests on a budget

blocks.p: A **package** is a set price that covers several things together, such as transport, a tour and lunch. An **itinerary** is a written plan of the trip showing the places and the times for each day.

ul: Ask what food the guest likes, the budget, how many people, the date and the time, and any special needs (vegetarian, allergies, high chairs, wheelchair access).
Suggest **a few good places** with their opening hours and prices, and offer transport.
When you book, tell the restaurant the **name, date, time, number in the party and any special needs**. Write the booking in the log and tell the guest.
Remember that restaurants may close on certain days; confirm the day and time.

head: Request
What to do
rows: Dry cleaning or laundry that the villa does not offer
Book a trusted outside dry cleaner, agree the cost and a **time for return**, and tell the guest. Record the items sent.
Babysitter
Use only a sitter from a **checked, trusted list**, with references. Agree the hours, the pay and the contact numbers, and ask the parents for any needs.
Snorkel gear or bicycle hire
Check that the shop is trusted and that the gear is **safe and clean**; check the price and deposit.
Hairdresser or massage
Use a licensed, approved provider; agree the time and price; explain what is included.
Special occasion (anniversary, birthday, wedding)
Ask for the date and wishes; pass the request to the right supplier, such as a baker, a florist or a photographer; confirm in writing.

blocks.note: Many tour companies pay the villa a commission. Choose the tour that suits the guest best, with honest information. Never recommend a supplier only because it pays you more.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: Guests are away from the villa and in places they do not know. Your advice can protect them. Safety must always come before price.

ul: Licensed operators have been checked for safety and insurance. They must supply **life jackets** for boat and water trips and seat belts in vehicles.
A man on the beach who offers a cheap boat trip, with no licence and no life jackets, is a **tout**. Politely advise the guests to use a licensed operator, and tell your supervisor or security.
If a guest still decides to go, tell your supervisor. Do not recommend or book it.

head: Tell the guest
Example
rows: Wear life jackets and seat belts
On boats, rafts, quad bikes and in cars
Follow the guide's instructions
Especially on rivers, caves and the sea
Take sun protection and water
Hat, sunscreen, bottle of water
Keep valuables safe
Leave passports and spare cash in the safe at the villa
Buy only from licensed vendors
Avoid pressure from street sellers
Alcohol and water do not mix
No alcohol before swimming, rafting or boating
Keep the villa's phone number
To call if there is a problem

blocks.p: The Atlantic **hurricane season** runs from June to November, and heavy rain and storms can happen at other times. When a **storm or hurricane warning** is given, check with the operator whether the trip will go ahead, and **update the guest**. Boat trips and river trips can be cancelled or delayed. Never encourage a guest to go in bad weather. Follow your manager's advice, and if you are unsure, check a reliable forecast or ask the tour desk.

ul: Check the minimum age and weight for rafting, ziplining, quad biking and boat trips.
Check that life jackets **fit the child**.
Ask the parents what the child can do, and whether they are comfortable.
Agree who will supervise the child during the trip.

blocks.note: If you have any doubt about the safety of a trip, do not book it. Your honest 'no' protects the guest and the villa.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: Guests rely on your advice. Give it for the guest's benefit, not for your own gain.
Refuse politely if a driver, tout or supplier offers you **money, gifts or favours** for sending guests, and **report it to your supervisor**.
Never hide a risk, and never say something is safe when you are not sure.
Deal calmly with touts: do not argue, guide guests towards licensed services, and tell security or the supervisor.
Never recommend a service you have not checked.

blocks.p: A sick guest can be frightened and alone. Stay calm and caring, act quickly and protect the guest's privacy. **You are not a doctor: never give medicine or diagnose.**

head: Situation
What to do
rows: A guest is not breathing normally, has collapsed, has chest pain, a heavy bleed, a head injury or severe allergic reaction
**Emergency.** Call an ambulance at once (**110** in Jamaica). Get a trained first aider. Stay with the guest. Tell the supervisor.
A guest feels unwell but it is not urgent (fever, stomach upset, sunburn, minor injury)
Ask what the guest needs, call a **doctor from the villa's approved list**, agree the time and fee, and tell the supervisor.
A guest needs medicine
Send them to a **licensed pharmacy** with the prescription; do not give tablets from the villa.
A guest needs the hospital
Arrange safe transport (an ambulance or a licensed taxi, as the doctor advises), and let someone go with them if the supervisor agrees.

blocks.note: In Jamaica, 110 is the number for the ambulance and the fire service, and 119 is the number for the police. Keep these numbers at the desk, with the numbers of the doctors, the nearest hospital and the pharmacies.
blocks.label: Jamaica

flow: Ask calmly what is wrong and what the guest wants
Decide: emergency or not?
Call the ambulance, or a doctor from the approved list
Tell the supervisor
Let the doctor and the guest speak in private
Help with the pharmacy or follow-up
Record the action

head: Term
Meaning
rows: House call
A doctor comes to see the guest at the villa instead of at the clinic
Prescription
A doctor's written order for medicine, which the guest takes to a pharmacy
Pharmacy
A licensed shop that sells medicine
First aider
A person trained to give first help until a doctor comes

ul: A guest's health is private. Share information **only with those who need to know**, such as the doctor and your supervisor.
Do not discuss it with other guests, other staff, or callers.
Keep notes secure, and write only what is needed in the log.
When the doctor visits, let the guest and doctor talk **in private**.

blocks.p: Jamaica's data protection law expects personal information, including health information, to be kept safe and used only for its purpose. If a tour company asks for guest details, give only what is needed: the name, the number of people and the pick-up place. Never give out the room number.

ol: Contact the supplier by phone or email. Give the details needed: the guest's name, date, time, number of people, pick-up place and any special needs.
Ask the price, what is included, the deposit and the **cancellation terms**.
Get a **booking number** from the supplier.
Write a **confirmation slip** for the guest.
Record the booking in the log.
Tell the supervisor if anything is unusual.

head: A confirmation slip shows
Example
rows: Guest name and room
Mr Peters, Villa 2 (not said aloud in public)
Service and supplier
Rafting trip, licensed operator
Date, pick-up time and place
Saturday 9:00 a.m., villa gate
Cost, currency and what is included
US$80 per person, lunch included
Booking number and contact
The supplier's number
Cancellation terms
Free until 24 hours before

blocks.p: Confirm a phone booking **in writing**. Book popular tours **as early as possible** once the guest agrees.

ul: Tell the guest the **full price, the currency, what is included, and any deposit or fees** before you book.
**Work out the total** and show the sum. Example: a tour costs US$80 per person and four guests go: 80 x 4 = **US$320**.
If the guest pays in the other currency, use **only the villa's rate for that day**, show the sum, and give a receipt.
If the guest pays through the villa: **count the cash**, give a **receipt showing the amount and the currency**, and hand the money in as the policy says.
If the guest wants the cost on the villa account: get the guest's **signature on a charge slip**.
Never add secret charges. Say clearly any fee the villa adds, and record every payment.

blocks.p: **Worked example (made-up rate).** A tour costs US$65 for each adult and US$40 for each child. A family has 2 adults and 2 children: 2 x 65 = 130 and 2 x 40 = 80, so the total is 130 + 80 = **US$210**. If the villa's rate is US$1 = J$155, then 210 x 155 = **J$32,550**.
Every outside booking is written in the **external services log** so that any staff member can check or follow it up. The log shows:

ul: the date the request was made, the guest and room
the service and the supplier, with the contact number
the date and time of the service and the number of people
the cost, the currency and how it was paid
the booking number, and who booked it (your name)
changes, problems and the follow-up

blocks.p: Keep confirmations and receipts. Records let anyone follow up, match payments to bookings, and settle disputes.

blocks.note: Keep forms with guest details out of sight, and shred them when they are no longer needed.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: If a guest wants to cancel a tour booked for tomorrow, check the **cancellation policy and any fee** before you phone the supplier. Tell the guest the fee, if there is one, and record the cancellation number.

flow: Act quickly: call the supplier with the booking number
Find out what has happened and how long
Arrange a licensed replacement, a new time or a refund
Tell the guest honestly and say sorry
Tell the supervisor
Record it and follow up

head: Problem
What to do
rows: The airport taxi is late
Call the transport company at once to find out where it is, and tell the guest. If the flight is near, arrange another licensed taxi.
The taxi has broken down
Arrange **another licensed taxi** immediately, tell the guest, and inform the supplier.
A tour is full or cancelled
Offer another day, another operator from the approved list, or a refund.
The weather turns bad
Check with the operator, update the guest and offer another day.
A restaurant has lost the booking
Apologise, call the restaurant, offer another place, and tell the guest.
The guest complains the tour guide was rude
**Listen, say sorry, record it and tell your supervisor**; pass the feedback to the supplier.

ul: Stay calm. Do not blame the guest or the supplier.
Say what you **can** do. Do not promise what you cannot control.
Keep the guest informed until it is solved.
Never ask the guest to solve the problem.

blocks.p: When guests return from a tour, ask **'How was it?'** and listen. This shows care, lets you put problems right, and helps you advise future guests. Pass on the feedback to your supervisor, and **review the supplier**: good suppliers stay on the list, and poor ones are removed.
A driver who offers money to send guests to him is trying to buy your advice. Refuse politely and **report it to your supervisor**. Honest advice builds trust, good reviews and repeat business.

blocks.note: Never take a commission, gift or favour from a supplier without your supervisor's knowledge and the property's policy. When in doubt, ask.
blocks.label: Remember

ul: explain what an external service is and give examples
ask open questions to find out a guest's needs, including special needs
explain why the villa uses an approved list of licensed suppliers, and what is checked
book an airport transfer with the right details, and work out a pick-up time
advise a guest who wants to rent a car about driving on the left, the licence and the deposit
explain private and shared tours, packages and itineraries
give the information a guest needs before a tour
give safety advice for boats, rafting and other trips, including weather and children
deal with touts and with offers of money from suppliers
arrange a doctor, a pharmacy or an ambulance, and keep health information private
book a restaurant, a babysitter, dry cleaning or hire equipment
tell the guest the price, the currency and the terms, and work out totals in US$ and J$
give a receipt, or get a signature on a charge slip
write a confirmation slip and the external services log
deal with a late taxi, a cancelled tour or a complaint, and follow up

terms: A service from an outside business, such as a tour or a taxi
The villa's list of licensed, checked suppliers
A booked ride between the airport and the villa
A person who arranges tours, transport and bookings for guests
A written plan of a trip, with the places and times
One set price that covers several things together
A tour for one party only
The number a supplier gives to find the booking again
Part of the price paid in advance to hold a booking
A doctor's written order for medicine
A doctor's visit to the guest at the villa
A person on the street who pushes unlicensed services
Money a supplier pays the villa for sending guests

c1.title: A departure flight from Montego Bay
c1.text: Mr and Mrs Winston Forbes are staying at a villa in Negril. Their flight leaves Sangster International Airport at 6:50 p.m. (18:50) on Sunday, and they must check in 3 hours before. The drive from Negril to the airport usually takes about 1 hour 15 minutes, and the villa likes to add 30 minutes for traffic. They have four bags and want a licensed driver. The villa's approved taxi charges J$9,000 each way, or US$60.

c2.title: A family wants to go river rafting
c2.text: Mrs Joy Dixon, her husband and their two children, aged 5 and 9, want a river rafting trip for Saturday. The tour costs US$65 for each adult and US$40 for each child, with lunch included. The operator's rule says that children must be at least 6 years old and weigh at least 18 kg. Mrs Dixon's mother, who walks with a stick, would like to come along.

c3.title: A guest who feels unwell in Port Antonio
c3.text: At 8 p.m. Mr Leonard Pryce, a guest at a villa in Port Antonio, tells receptionist Kimberly that he has a fever and a stomach upset since lunch, and he asks for a doctor. He is awake and talking normally. Later, a man phones from a tour company, says he is Mr Pryce's friend, and asks what is wrong with him.

c4.title: A tout and an offer on the beach
c4.text: A man at the gate of a villa in Treasure Beach offers some guests a cheap quad-bike tour on his own bikes. He has no licence, no insurance and no helmets. The same day a taxi driver offers the receptionist J$5,000 a week to send all the villa's guests to him. A guest also asks the receptionist to recommend the best tour in the area.

c5.title: A taxi that does not come
c5.text: The airport taxi booked for the Chin family has not arrived. Their flight leaves in three hours. The receptionist phones the company, which says the taxi has broken down. Mr Chin is worried and asks for a refund. Later a storm warning is given, and the operator cancels another guest's boat trip for the next day.

questions.q: By what time must the Forbes family be at the airport to check in?
questions.why: Check-in is 3 hours before the 6:50 p.m. flight, so 6:50 - 3:00 = 3:50 p.m.

questions.q: The drive is 1 hour 15 minutes, plus a 30-minute buffer. What is the latest time the driver should collect them?
questions.why: They need to arrive at 3:50 p.m. Subtract the drive and the buffer: 1:15 + 0:30 = 1:45, and 3:50 - 1:45 = 2:05 p.m.

questions.q: Which details must the receptionist give the transport company when booking?
o: The room rate and the number of nights the guests have stayed
The guests' passport numbers and the names of their children
Names, flight, time, number of people and bags
The hotel's bank details and the date of the guests' arrival
questions.why: A transfer booking needs the flight, date and time, the number of people and bags and where to collect them. Passport numbers and bank details are not needed.

questions.q: The taxi charges J$9,000 each way. What is the cost of both ways?
questions.why: 9,000 x 2 = J$18,000. Tell the guests the price and the currency before you book.

questions.q: What is the total cost for Mr and Mrs Dixon and their 9-year-old, if the 5-year-old cannot go?
questions.why: Two adults x US$65 = US$130, plus one child at US$40 = US$170. Check each person's age and weight against the operator's rules.

questions.q: Why can the 5-year-old not go on the rafting trip?
o: The tour company only takes children who have been rafting before
The operator's minimum age is 6, and life jackets must fit
Children are never allowed on river trips in Jamaica
The trip costs too much for a child of that age
questions.why: Operators set a minimum age and weight for safety, and life jackets must fit. Tell the parents honestly and offer a suitable alternative.

questions.q: What is the best alternative for the 5-year-old and the grandmother, who walks with a stick?
o: Tell them to wait at the villa while the others go on the trip
Ask the operator to ignore the age rule for the younger child
Offer a gentler activity that suits them, such as a short, easy visit
Book them on the trip, and tell them to stay in the middle of the raft
questions.why: Find out what suits the guests and offer a suitable choice. Never ignore safety rules or book unsuitable trips.

questions.q: Mrs Dixon asks you to charge the tour to the villa account. What should you get?
o: A deposit of one night's room cost in cash
Her husband's phone number on the booking form
A promise that she will pay at check-out
The guest's signature on a charge slip
questions.why: A guest's signature on a charge slip shows that she agreed to the charge, and protects the villa and the guest.

questions.q: Mr Pryce has a fever but is awake and talking normally. What should Kimberly do?
o: Call a doctor from the approved list and tell the supervisor
Give him fever tablets from the villa's first aid box to start with
Tell him to wait until morning and see how he feels then
Send him to the hospital alone in a taxi, without telling anyone
questions.why: This is not an emergency. Use the approved doctor list, agree the time and fee, tell the supervisor and never give medicine yourself.

questions.q: Which sign would turn this into an emergency?
o: He asks for a second blanket
He collapses or cannot breathe normally
He says he is hungry
He asks for a quiet room
questions.why: A collapse or trouble breathing is an emergency: call an ambulance (110) and a first aider at once.

questions.q: The man from the tour company asks what is wrong with Mr Pryce. How should Kimberly reply?
o: Say that Mr Pryce has a fever and a stomach upset, so the friend can send help
Say that the doctor is on the way to see him, without giving the name
Say she cannot give out guest information, and offer to take a message
Give the man the room number so that he can phone the guest himself
questions.why: A guest's health and room number are private. Offer to take a message and tell the guest.

questions.q: When the doctor arrives, how should the privacy of the guest be protected?
o: Stay in the room to help the doctor and to answer all of his questions
Tell the other staff what is wrong with him, so that they can help
Write the full details in the front desk log for all staff to read
Let the doctor and guest talk in private, and share only what is needed
questions.why: Health information is shared only with those who need to know. The guest and the doctor should speak in private.

questions.q: The man at the gate has no licence, insurance or helmets. What should the receptionist advise the guests?
o: Book a licensed operator that supplies helmets, and report the tout
Go with him if the price is cheap and the roads are dry that day
Take two helmets from the villa to use on the quad-bike tour
Choose any bike at the gate, but pay only after the tour is over
questions.why: Unlicensed operators are not checked for safety or insurance. Advise guests to use a licensed operator, and report the tout.

questions.q: The driver offers J$5,000 a week. What should the receptionist do?
o: Accept if the driver is a good one and the guests are happy
Refuse politely and report it to her supervisor
Accept but share the money with the other staff
Refuse, but say nothing about it to anyone
questions.why: Staff must not take money to send guests to a supplier. Report the offer, so that the villa can decide what to do.

questions.q: How should the receptionist choose which tour to recommend to the guest?
o: By which company pays the villa the biggest commission each month
By which tour is the most expensive and sounds the best of all
By what suits the guest, with honest information
By which company telephoned the villa most recently about it
questions.why: Advice must suit the guest. A commission may exist, but it must never decide the recommendation.

questions.q: The taxi has broken down and the flight leaves in three hours. What is the best next step?
o: Tell the Chins to find a taxi on the road for themselves
Wait for the taxi company to phone back with more news
Cancel the transfer and refund the Chins' money straight away
Arrange another licensed taxi at once and tell the Chins
questions.why: The guests must still reach the airport. Arrange a replacement from licensed taxis, tell them honestly and record the problem.

questions.q: Mr Chin asks for a refund. What should the receptionist do?
o: Apologise, record the problem and refer the refund to the supervisor
Promise the refund at once, to calm Mr Chin and keep him happy
Say that refunds are never possible for a late or broken taxi
Ask the taxi company to give the refund to him in cash on the spot
questions.why: Refunds are decided by the supervisor. Apologise, record the problem, and follow up with the supplier.

questions.q: The operator cancels the guest's boat trip because of the storm. What should the receptionist offer?
o: Nothing, because the weather is not the operator's fault at all
Another day, another activity or a refund, under its terms
A trip with a cheaper operator who is still going out today
A promise that the sea will be calm on the following day
questions.why: A cancelled trip should be rebooked, replaced or refunded under the supplier's terms. Tell the guest honestly and record it. Never push a guest to a cheaper, unsafe operator.

questions.q: Which record should the receptionist complete for the broken-down taxi?
o: Only the guest's folio, with the cost of the new taxi
Nothing, because the taxi was the supplier's problem
The external services log, with the problem and the replacement taxi
A note on the desk that is thrown away after the shift
questions.why: Every outside booking, change and problem goes in the external services log, so that any staff member can follow it up and the supplier can be reviewed.

questions.q: What does the villa do after a guest returns from a tour?
o: Wait for the guest to send an email before saying anything
Only ask if the guest looks unhappy or upset
Record the cost, but not the guest's comments or complaints
Ask how it went and pass on the feedback
questions.why: Asking guests how their tour went shows care, puts problems right and helps the villa review suppliers and advise future guests.
